docker.name: Docker
docker.not_running: Docker is not running. Start Docker Desktop and scan again.
docker.image_used: Used by {{.Count}} container(s). Remove those containers first.
docker.volume_attached: Attached to {{.Count}} container(s). Remove those containers first.
docker.containers.title: Containers
docker.containers.what: Containers that have been created on this Mac, running or stopped.
docker.containers.why: A stopped container is usually leftover from an old docker run. Running containers can't be selected.
docker.containers.after: Files written inside the container (not into a volume) are lost. The image stays and can start a new container.
docker.images.title: Images
docker.images.what: Downloaded or built container images. The size shown is what deleting frees: layers shared with other images stay.
docker.images.why: Images can be pulled or built again. Images used by any container can't be selected.
docker.images.after: The next docker run or compose up downloads or rebuilds the image.
docker.volumes.title: Volumes
docker.volumes.what: Storage that containers keep between restarts, often databases.
docker.volumes.why: Volumes not attached to any container are usually left from removed projects. Attached volumes can't be selected.
docker.volumes.after: Data in the volume is lost for good. Check that it isn't a database you still need.
docker.build_cache.title: Build cache
docker.build_cache.what: Intermediate layers saved by docker build to speed up the next build.
docker.build_cache.why: Only cache that no build is using right now is removed. Docker recreates it.
docker.build_cache.after: The next docker build of each image runs all steps from scratch.
